label: GLBP
notes: Cisco Gateway Load Balancing Protocol over UDP port 3222, sent to 224.0.0.102 from the router's own interface address (both UDP ports 3222, TTL 255). Cisco never published a packet specification; the layout follows Wireshark's reverse-engineered packet-glbp.c dissector, confirmed byte for byte against live captures. The 12-byte fixed header is modelled in full: the owner MAC is the sending router's interface MAC ("Owner ID" in show glbp output), payload-embedded and therefore a first-class mac field. Everything after byte 12 is a TLV chain (Hello with gateway state, priority, millisecond timers and the virtual address; forwarder request/response with the virtual MAC; MD5 or clear-text authentication) whose offsets shift with each TLV, so no TLV field sits at a fixed offset. This completes the first-hop redundancy trio with hsrp and vrrp; unlike them GLBP load-shares across up to four virtual forwarders per group.

fields.label: Version
fields.ref: GLBP header layout (Cisco proprietary, unpublished; Wireshark packet-glbp.c)
fields.description: GLBP version; 1 in every observed deployment.

fields.label: Undocumented Control Byte
fields.ref: GLBP header layout (Cisco proprietary, unpublished; Wireshark packet-glbp.c)
fields.description: Semantics undocumented; 0 on Hello datagrams, 1 and 2 observed on virtual-forwarder request/response exchanges (Wireshark's "Unknown1", bounded to at most 4 by its heuristic).

fields.label: Group
fields.ref: GLBP header layout (Cisco proprietary, unpublished; Wireshark packet-glbp.c)
fields.description: GLBP group number (0-1023 on Cisco); the virtual gateway and its up-to-four virtual forwarders share it.

fields.label: Undocumented Word
fields.ref: GLBP header layout (Cisco proprietary, unpublished; Wireshark packet-glbp.c)
fields.description: Semantics undocumented; zero in every observed packet (Wireshark's "Unknown2").

fields.label: Owner ID
fields.ref: GLBP header layout (Cisco proprietary, unpublished; Wireshark packet-glbp.c)
fields.description: The sending router's interface MAC address ("Owner ID" in show glbp output); the election identifies routers by it. Payload-embedded, so it is a first-class mac field rather than a host primitive.
